A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 23-page AgentBreeder paper, including Appendices A–E. The complete material supports comparison; pages 2–23 have identical extracted text, page drawing instructions, and rendered pixels.

before.justification: v2 reports original blue-team, red-team, and capability-only evolutionary experiments, with quantitative results in Tables 1–3 and evolutionary plots in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and their capability, safety, and helpfulness results in Section 5, Tables 1–3, and Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Section 4, and Appendices C–D retain identical evolutionary procedures, clustering, Pareto selection, mutation, crossover, prompts, and example scaffold code.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DROP, MMLU, GPQA, attack-enhanced SaladData, and TruthfulQA. Dataset, task, domain, and test-scenario coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same seed-scaffold comparators and ADAS comparisons within their corresponding experiments. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Model choices, evolutionary budgets, sampling procedures, and scoring protocols are identical. Tables 1–2 retain evaluations over 250 held-out samples, while Table 3 retains 500.

E4.justification: The single-objective ablation in Section 5.3, reward-hacking/helpfulness analysis in Section 5.1, and evolutionary analyses in Appendix A and Figures 2–3 are unchanged.

E5.justification: The 95% confidence intervals, bootstrap procedure description, and experimental run-count information are identical. No statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and results depicted in Figures 2–3 are unchanged. The reported capability, safety, and helpfulness findings and rankings are also retained.

T1.justification: Sections 2 and 4.5 retain identical definitions of Pareto optimality and Pareto fronts. No formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same attack, defense, and evaluation contributions and the same claims about capability and safety.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reward hacking, unsafe but capable scaffolds, and multi-objective optimization are unchanged. The limitations, future-work qualifications, and dual-use discussion are also identical.

D1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain identical implementation and model settings. Appendices C–E retain the same prompts, scaffold code, and experiment costs, and the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The background, related work, and reference list are identical, including the positioning relative to ADAS, MAP-Elites, and other agent-design and safety research.

P1.justification: v3 removes 'Meta AI' from Jakob Nicolaus Foerster's affiliations and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body language, section order, and appendix text are unchanged.

P2.justification: Removing the affiliation moves the remaining 'FLAIR, University of Oxford' line upward in the first-page author block; the arXiv stamp also changes. All figures, tables, captions, and pages 2–23 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 only changes an author affiliation and the version notice, with a small first-page layout adjustment. The scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility material, including all appendices, are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
